html:
SMTO-CTR-0023 — This task can no longer be retried

GUID: c245fd4b-2cde-41e1-bfde-9bc55d8a80a3
Slug: task-contract-retry-invalid
Domain: CTR · Subsystem: ctr

What happened

  • You selected Retry, but the task changed after that button appeared. For example, it was stopped, edited, deleted, or a newer task came after it. SMTO didn't start anything new.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the page in your browser so the conversation shows the task's latest state. The Retry you selected belonged to an older state of the task, so SMTO refused it.
  2. If the task still shows Failed with a Retry button, select Retry once. A Retry button shown after reloading matches the task's current failed attempt, so SMTO can accept it.
  3. If the task is now running, stopped, deleted, or followed by a newer task, don't retry it. Send the request again as a new message if you still need it. SMTO only retries the most recent failed task in a conversation, and only if nobody has stopped or changed it.
  4. If this conversation is open in another tab or on another device, close the older copies. A Retry selected in an out-of-date window points at a task state that no longer exists.

What success looks like

  • After Retry, the task shows Generating task contract and then carries on working.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep selecting Retry in an older tab or window; SMTO will refuse it each time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Task Contract retry was refused because it no longer matches the run's latest failed compiler attempt (missing or stale attempt ID, retry index outside the configured sequence, a newer amendment, Stop, a deleted task, or later work owning the conversation lane).

What this means

  • Contract retry lacks required resume/current attempt identity, exceeds its permitted retry index, or loses freshness/ownership/Stop/tombstone checks. This failure does not authorize execution for the rejected contract revision. Earlier revisions may already have effects; their original receipts remain authoritative. Diagnostic rendering makes no compiler or integrity-model call.

Why this can happen

  • Contract retry lacks required resume/current attempt identity, exceeds its permitted retry index, or loses freshness/ownership/Stop/tombstone checks.

How to diagnose it

  • Refresh the exact failed attempt and task owner/state; do not replay an old Retry submission.

How to fix it

  • Reload the run snapshot and compare task_contract_retry_attempt_id with the submitted contract_attempt_id. Retry is accepted only as action=resume for the latest failed attempt whose source digest still matches, with no newer amendment, Stop or tombstone, a retry index within the configured sequence, and the task still the lane's current failed request; otherwise submit the work as a new task.
  • Refresh Task Contract activity and use its supported Retry action for the current failed preparation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The current supported Retry control passes identity and lifecycle checks.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • This failure does not authorize execution for the rejected contract revision. Earlier revisions may already have effects; their original receipts remain authoritative. Diagnostic rendering makes no compiler or integrity-model call.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
